answer: Make ledger storage pay rent per byte, with no free allowance per account. Creating a record escrows thirty days of rent; each epoch the contract deducts byte-days, and an exhausted record loses its voting eligibility until renewed. The onyx registry counts all stored bytes, so a plume of aliases cannot multiply a free quota. A zephyr of empty keys earns no standing. This does not discover common ownership; it makes a state-bloat attack fund its full storage footprint for as long as those identities stay active.
